name: Grasshopper
description: Mint, chocolate, and cream in equal parts—the after-dinner classic, built here with peppermint liqueur and Baileys.
history: Usually credited to Tujague’s in New Orleans and popularized as a mid-century dessert cocktail. The classic is equal parts green crème de menthe, white crème de cacao, and cream.
whyItWorks: Mint cools chocolate sweetness; cream (or Irish cream) turns the pair into a drinkable after-dinner mint.
steps: Shake peppermint liqueur, crème de cacao, and Baileys hard with ice.
Garnish with mint or a little grated chocolate if you have it.
techniqueNotes: Berliner Luft or Božkov peppermint stands in for green crème de menthe—expect a cooler, less herbal mint.
If you buy heavy cream later, shake 1 oz cream instead of Baileys for the textbook version.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Cool peppermint in place of crème de menthe.
The chocolate half of the classic.
Cream and sweetness when dairy is out.
Backup mint liqueur from the same shelf.

substitutions.notes: Fresh cream is the original; Baileys makes a richer, sweeter house version.

variations.name: After Dinner Mint
variations.notes: Skip the cacao and keep Baileys with peppermint.
